summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with mode 1777 (world read/write/execute + sticky bit), owned by root:root. Verified functionally with two separate unprivileged users: both could write files into the directory, but only the file owner (not another user) could delete a file, matching sticky-bit semantics. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via native `reboot`, polled until reconnection, confirmed a changed boot_id (new boot), and re-verified both the directory permissions and the cross-user delete-restriction behavior post-reboot were unchanged. All test users and files were cleaned up, leaving /srv/drop empty.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv and confirmed /srv/drop did not exist
Created /srv/drop with mkdir, chmod 1777, chown root:root
Verified SELinux context (var_t, enforcing) did not block access
Created two temporary test users and verified both could write to /srv/drop
Verified that one user could not remove a file owned by the other user (rm failed with Operation not permitted)
Verified the file owner could remove their own file
Cleaned up test files and users
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, directory permissions, systemd health
Triggered a native reboot of node1 via backgrounded `reboot` command so the ack returned first
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed after reboot, proving an actual restart
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions (1777, root:root) persisted after reboot
Re-ran the cross-user write/delete functional test post-reboot with a fresh pair of test users, confirming identical sticky-bit behavior
Cleaned up final test users and files, leaving /srv/drop empty

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as shared writable directory with sticky bit (users cannot remove others' files)
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/drop did not exist, then created it with mode 1777 root:root; ls/stat show drwxrwxrwt with sticky bit (t) set

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: any user can write, only owner can delete their own file
evidence.summary: Two unprivileged users (dropuser1, dropuser2) both wrote files into /srv/drop; dropuser2's rm on dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit=1), while dropuser1 could delete their own file (exit=0)

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts before finishing
evidence.summary: Removed lingering user sessions/processes and deleted temporary test users; /srv/drop left empty with correct 1777 root:root ownership
Captured boot_id 739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc, uptime since 2026-09-29 10:19:38, directory perms 1777 root:root, systemctl is-system-running=running
Backgrounded `reboot` command via nohup+disown returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts/reset during reboot, then successful reconnection with new boot_id e3ddf5d0-41be-4e08-bf31-efeb9ca44d99, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required configuration and functional behavior
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop retained mode 1777 root:root, system running, SELinux enforcing; fresh cross-user test (dropuserA/dropuserB) reproduced identical sticky-bit behavior (cross-user rm denied, owner rm succeeded)
